nodes.description: The two reported families carry variants in different parts of the protein, and the node is named generically so it does not assert one lesion for both. The founding family is homozygous for c.6799G>A, predicting p.D2267N in the C-type lectin domain of aggrecan's G3 domain; that identification constrains what kind of mechanism this is, since the locus was mapped by identity-by-descent to a 17.4 Mb interval containing 296 genes and ranking those genes by cartilage-selective expression left only two, of which ACAN was one. The substituted residue is predicted to coordinate a calcium ion that shapes the binding loops of the lectin domain, and it is this allele that carries the functional work downstream. The second patient instead carries two missense variants in the chondroitin sulfate CS1 and CS2 domains, assessed only in silico. The mechanistic arms below are established for the lectin-domain allele; what the CS-domain variants do is not known.

nodes.description: The functional lesion. Surface plasmon resonance showed the substitution changes both the affinity and the kinetics of the interaction between the aggrecan G3 domain and tenascin-C. The G3 lectin domain is how aggrecan engages the wider matrix network - tenascin-R and tenascin-C, fibulins, fibrillin-1 - all in a calcium-dependent manner, so a change at the calcium-coordinating residue degrades the anchoring rather than the molecule.

nodes.description: Linear bone growth is produced by chondrocyte division and matrix production at the growth plate, then replacement of that cartilage by bone. A defective matrix compromises both the template and the mechanical environment the chondrocytes work in. Because the vertebral bodies, epiphyses and metaphyses are all sites of endochondral growth, one lesion at this node produces the combined spondylar, epiphyseal and metaphyseal picture the disease is named for - which is why this is a single dysplasia rather than three coincident ones.

nodes.description: A negative result, and a load-bearing one. Expressing normal and mutant G3 domains in mammalian cells showed the mutation created a new functional N-glycosylation site but did not impair trafficking or secretion. That rules out the mechanisms this disease would otherwise be assumed to have - haploinsufficiency, retention in the endoplasmic reticulum, degradation of a misfolded product - and forces the mechanism onto what the secreted protein then fails to do.
